title: Noisy influence as a derivative norm
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $\rho\ge0$. Then the noisy influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$ equals $\|T_{\sqrt{\rho}}D_i f\|_2^2$, where $(D_i f)(x)=\bigl(f(x^{i\mapsto0})-f(x^{i\mapsto1})\bigr)/2$ and the norm is taken with respect to the uniform measure on the cube.
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $i\in[n]$, and $\rho\ge0$. Then $I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\|T_{\sqrt\rho}D_if\|_2^2$, where $D_if(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$.
